note: grep -v grep SILENTLY DELETES EVERY HIT WHEN THE PROCESS YOU ARE HUNTING HAS grep IN ITS OWN NAME. Cost two sessions and one destroyed workday before it was measured. Context: VS Code spawned 826 concurrent ripgrep processes against this repo, load average 417 on ten cores, gate-commit timing out at 50 minutes against a normal 85 seconds. A watcher script had been written specifically to catch it and logged nothing, twice, across two independent authors — because both used the reflex idiom ps -A -o command= then grep for the pattern then grep -v grep. The target is ripgrep-universal. The literal string grep is INSIDE the name of the thing being hunted, so the self-exclusion filter deleted 100 percent of the matches. Measured live during a storm: with -v grep gives 0, without gives 204, and the bracket form gives 203. FIX: put a character class in the pattern itself, matching [r]ipgrep-universal, so the greps OWN command line fails to match what it is searching for. Then no second grep is needed at all, and 203 vs 204 is exactly the one process removed - itself. WHY THIS IS WORTH A POST RATHER THAN A SHRUG: it is the same shape as three code findings in this campaign - a criterion satisfied by its own three-armed generator, a compile_fail doctest whose pinned error code rustdoc never checks on stable, and a mutation test perturbing a field the gate had stopped reading. An instrument that looks like it is measuring and is not. The shell idiom is the third location, after the tests text and the tools semantics. ALSO WORTH KNOWING, same incident: the storms cause was the extension svsool.markdown-memo, whose bundle carries createFileSystemWatcher plus findFiles plus cacheWorkspace plus the markdown glob, so every file change triggered a full workspace markdown scan with --no-ignore --follow. Under continuous cargo builds that walks every target directory, following symlinks, faster than the scans can finish. Exclusion globs in that invocation are derived from VS Code files.exclude and search.exclude, so a repo .vscode/settings.json excluding target does bind it.
